'''Kelan Dewayne Martin''' (born August 3, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He attended [[Ballard High School (Louisville, Kentucky)|Ballard High School]] in [[Louisville, Kentucky]], and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler Bulldogs]], where he scored 2,047 points during his career, the second highest in the school's history. Martin was selected for the All-Big East second team on two occasions, the All-District 5 second team by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]], and as a senior, he was named to the [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] first team.

==Early life==
Martin comes from a basketball family. His father, Kenneth, was on the state championship team at Louisville's [[Ballard High School (Louisville, Kentucky)|Ballard High School]] and won an [[NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament|NCAA Division II championship]] at [[Kentucky Wesleyan]]. His mother, the former Kristie Jordan, was honored with a retired jersey at Ballard and competed for an NCAA runner-up team at [[Western Kentucky Lady Toppers basketball|Western Kentucky]]. They met at the age of eight growing up in [[housing projects]] in downtown Louisville and married after college. As of 2017 Kenneth works as assistant director of pupil personnel for [[Jefferson County Public Schools (Kentucky)|Jefferson County Public Schools]], while Kristie works in administration monitoring Louisville's police budget. Kelan has a younger brother, Kameron, and was raised with cousin Jalil Brown, the son of Kristie's deceased sister.<ref name="shadows">{{cite news|last=Woods|first=David|title=Butler's Kelan Martin: Out of the shadows and into the spotlight|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2016/11/07/butlers-kelan-martin-out-shadows-and-into-spotlight/93141196/|access-date=July 4, 2017|work=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|date=November 7, 2016|archive-date=December 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181222130920/https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2016/11/07/butlers-kelan-martin-out-shadows-and-into-spotlight/93141196/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Growing up, Kelan preferred American football to basketball. He competed for Louisville Legends summer teams in middle school, where he was nicknamed "Baby Shaq" by [[Rajon Rondo]]. While at Ballard High School, he competed for the AAU team Indiana Elite, where future [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] player Quentin Snider starred. Martin measured {{Height|ft=6|in=5|abbr=mos}} as a freshman at Ballard and started several games. He stopped playing football as a sophomore and worked on improving his running ability. As a junior, Martin guided Ballard to the Sweet 16 of the Kentucky basketball tournament, recording 23 [[Point (basketball)|point]]s and 14 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s in the Bruins' 59–55 victory over [[Montgomery County High School (Kentucky)|Montgomery County]] at [[Rupp Arena]]. In the championship, Martin scored 19 points and pulled down 12 rebounds, but [[Madison County Schools (Kentucky)|Madison County]] beat Ballard 65–64.<ref name="shadows"/> He averaged 19.1 points and 10.2 rebounds as a junior and was named to the Second Team All-State.<ref name="butler"/>

Coach Chris Renner called Martin's senior year the best season of any player he coached at Ballard. The Bruins were ranked number one in Kentucky. Although outshone by Quentin Snider, Martin scored 16 points in an overtime loss to [[Trey Lyles]]-led [[Arsenal Technical High School|Arsenal Tech]]. He had 28 points, including the deciding [[three-pointer]], when Ballard beat [[Myles Turner (basketball)|Myles Turner]] and [[Trinity High School (Euless, Texas)]] 72–70.<ref name="shadows"/> In another game against Doss High School, Martin scored 36 points,<ref name="butler">{{cite web|title=30 Kelan Martin|url=http://butlersports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4090|website=[[Butler Bulldogs]]|access-date=July 4, 2017|archive-date=June 27, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170627232029/http://butlersports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4090|url-status=live}}</ref> and coach Renner started isolating him from practices since he overwhelmed team scrimmages. The season ended when the Bruins lost to [[Trinity High School (Louisville)]] in the regional championship 59–58.<ref name="shadows"/> He scored 2,014 points in his career, third in school history. As a senior, Martin averaged 22.8 points and 8.7 rebounds per game, shooting 37 percent from three-point range.<ref name="butler"/>

His first recruiting offer was from [[IUPUI Jaguars men's basketball|IUPUI]], coached by his father's high school teammate [[Todd Howard (basketball)|Todd Howard]]. Martin was first recruited to Butler by [[Brad Stevens]], and his recruitment continued under [[Brandon Miller (basketball, born 1979)|Brandon Miller]]. He considered [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], [[St. Louis Billikens men's basketball|St. Louis]], [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] and [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] but chose Butler because he liked the coaches and players. When Quentin Snider decommitted from [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] and selected Louisville, Martin's friends thought he should follow suit but he remained firm in his commitment to the Bulldogs. He was ranked 139th nationally by Rivals.com and was a finalist for [[Kentucky Mr. Basketball]].<ref name="shadows"/>

==College career==
===Freshman season (2014–2015)===
By the time Martin arrived on campus, [[Chris Holtmann]] was the coach.<ref name="shadows"/> On November 22, 2014, Martin had a season-high 23 points to go along with seven rebounds in a win over [[Loyola Greyhounds men's basketball|Loyola (Maryland)]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Butler crushes Loyola (MD), 80-39|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400587047|access-date=July 4, 2017|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 22, 2014|archive-date=December 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201035451/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400587047|url-status=live}}</ref> The following game, Martin had 17 points in 17 minutes in a 74–66 upset over fifth-ranked [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Butler hangs on for upset of No. 5 North Carolina in Battle 4 Atlantis|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400587794|access-date=July 4, 2017|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 26, 2014|archive-date=December 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201044106/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400587794|url-status=live}}</ref> He was named Big East Rookie of the Week on March 9, 2015, after scoring 14 points against [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]]. Martin averaged 7.1 points and 2.1 rebounds in 14.5 minutes per game.<ref name="butler"/>

==Professional career==

===Riesen Ludwigsburg (2018–2019)===
Prior to the [[2018 NBA draft]],  Martin worked out for 12 NBA teams. After going undrafted, he signed a Summer League deal with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=VanTryon |first=Matthew |last2=Woods |first2=David |name-list-style=amp |title=Kelan Martin signs Summer League contract with Utah Jazz |language=en |work=Indianapolis Star |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2018/06/22/butlers-kelan-martin-signs-summer-league-contract-utah-jazz/727551002/ |url-status=live |access-date=June 26, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028175004/https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2018/06/22/butlers-kelan-martin-signs-summer-league-contract-utah-jazz/727551002/ |archive-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref> On July 31, 2018, Martin signed with [[MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Lupo |first=Nicola |title=Kelan Martin signs with MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/germany/bbl/284117/kelan-martin-signs-with-mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180807063423/https://sportando.basketball/en/germany/bbl/284117/kelan-martin-signs-with-mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.html |archive-date=August 7, 2018 |access-date=August 6, 2018 |website=Sportando}}</ref> Martin averaged 13.7 points and 4.4 rebounds per game in 27 games in Germany.<ref name="fox">{{cite news |title=No two-ways about it, rookie Martin shining in recent stint with Wolves |url=https://www.foxsports.com/north/story/minnesota-timberwolves-young-player-tracker-kelan-martin-karl-anthony-towns-jarrett-culver-112119 |access-date=December 10, 2019 |work=[[Fox Sports]] |date=November 21, 2019 |archive-date=December 11, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211042353/https://www.foxsports.com/north/story/minnesota-timberwolves-young-player-tracker-kelan-martin-karl-anthony-towns-jarrett-culver-112119 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2019–2020)===
Martin joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]], and after impressing for the team, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web |last=Flood |first=Sam |date=August 9, 2019 |title=Timberwolves Sign Kelan Martin to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-kelan-martin-two-way-contract |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190809220255/https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-kelan-martin-two-way-contract |archive-date=August 9, 2019 |access-date=August 9, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He made his NBA debut on October 15 but was inactive in the next nine games. [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on December 28.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kelan Martin drops career-high 17 points in Saturday's loss ===Indiana Pacers (2020–2022)===
On November 26, 2020, Martin signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |last=VanTryon |first=Matthew |title=Former Butler Bulldog Kelan Martin signs with Pacers |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2020/11/26/kelan-martin-signs-indiana-pacers-butler-bulldogs/6432849002/ |access-date=November 26, 2020 |work=[[Indianapolis Star]] |date=November 26, 2020 |archive-date=November 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126173829/https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2020/11/26/kelan-martin-signs-indiana-pacers-butler-bulldogs/6432849002/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-seven-players|title=Pacers Sign Seven Players|work=NBA.com|date=November 29, 2020|access-date=November 30, 2020|archive-date=November 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130043217/https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-seven-players|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored a then-season-high 11 points off the bench in 104–93 loss against the [[Sacramento Kings]] on May 5, 2021. On May 10, 2021, Martin scored a new career high of 25 points against the Cleveland Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite news |title=Pacers beat Cavaliers 111-102, move into ninth place in the East |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401307834 |access-date=May 11, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=May 10, 2021 |archive-date=May 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511211856/https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401307834 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On January 6, 2022, Martin was waived by the Pacers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pacers Waive Kelan Martin|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-kelan-martin|url-status=live|access-date=January 6, 2022|website=Indiana Pacers|archive-date=January 6, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220106211015/https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-kelan-martin}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2022)===
On February 23, 2022, Martin signed a 10-day contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Boston Celtics|number=1496534679641591810|title=We have signed forwards Malik Fitts and Kelan Martin to 10-day contracts.|user=celtics|date=February 23, 2022|access-date=February 23, 2022}}</ref> He signed a second 10-day contract on March 5.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 4, 2022 |title=Celtics' Kelan Martin: Slated to sign another 10-day deal |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-kelan-martin-slated-to-sign-another-10-day-deal/ |access-date=March 17, 2022 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref>

===Grand Rapids Gold (2022)===
On March 18, 2022, Martin was acquired via available player pool by the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=March 18, 2022|access-date=March 18, 2022}}</ref> On March 25, he was waived.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021-22 Grand Rapids Gold Transactions |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Grand-Rapids-Gold/63/Transaction_History/2022 |access-date=March 27, 2022 |website=RealGM}}</ref>

===Birmingham Squadron (2022–2023)===
On November 4, 2022, Martin was named to the opening-night roster for the [[Birmingham Squadron]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/birmingham-squadron-announce-opening-night-roster/n-5895676|website=oursportscentral.com|title=Birmingham Squadron Announce Opening Night Roster|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}}</ref>

===Pınar Karşıyaka (2023–2024)===
On June 28, 2023, Martin signed with [[Pınar Karşıyaka]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Skerletic |first=Dario |date=June 28, 2023 |title=Pinar Karsiyaka inks Kelan Martin |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/pinar-karsiyaka-inks-kelan-martin/ |access-date=June 28, 2023 |website=sportando.basketball}}</ref>

===Beşiktaş (2024–2025)===
On June 27, 2024, Martin signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Emlakjet]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=BJK_Basketbol |number=1806294572768600502 |title=Kelan Martin Beşiktaş’ta}}</ref>

===UCAM Murcia (2026)===
In January 2026, Martin signed for [[UCAM Murcia CB|UCAM Murcia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and [[FIBA Europe Cup|Europe Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |date=January 8, 2026 |title=Kelan Martin, un 4 con recursos para el UCAM Murcia |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/541429-kelan-martin-un-4-con-recursos-para-el-ucam-murcia.html |access-date=January 8, 2026 |website=acb.com |language=es}}</ref>

===Illawarra Hawks (2026–present)===
On August 7, 2026, Martin signed with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2026–27 NBL season|2026–27 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Illawarra Hawks sign Kelan Martin for NBL27 {{!}} Illawarra Hawks |url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/illawarra-hawks-sign-kelan-martin-for-nbl27 |access-date=7 August 2026 |work=www.hawks.com.au |date=7 August 2026 |language=en}}</ref>
